era.basis: Origin of the term: Karpathy's Feb 2, 2025 tweet that coined 'vibe coding'; self-report is definitional of the post-vibe era.

provenance.reputation: Capability corroborated: ex-Director of AI at Tesla, founding member of OpenAI, well-known deep-learning educator — the over-trust stance is stated in his own words, proving high D1 does not imply rigor.

evidence_quotes.quote: There's a new kind of coding I call 'vibe coding', where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, and forget that the code even exists.
I 'Accept All' always, I don't read the diffs anymore. When I get error messages I just copy paste them in with no comment, usually that fixes it.
It's not too bad for throwaway weekend projects, but still quite amusing.

behavioral_prediction: On a throwaway weekend project this expert dumps loose voice-driven prompts at the agent, accepts every diff unread, and on errors just pastes the message back and re-runs rather than inspecting the code himself.

evidence_quotes.quote: Employing stricter typings that explicitly prohibit invalid states can significantly guide AI agents toward producing higher quality and more correct code.
Well-defined types act as guardrails and guides, not just for human developers, but for our AI partners too, leading to more robust, maintainable, and correct software, faster.
When the AI hallucinated, the TypeScript type system forced rapid iteration and correction
Thanks to these stricter typings, the agent could also self-correct more effectively when it made mistakes, using TypeScript's error messages.

behavioral_prediction: Will reject agent output that widens types or leaks `any`, demand discriminated unions that make illegal states unrepresentable, and lean on compiler errors to force iterative self-correction rather than trusting generated code on sight.

evidence_quotes.quote: I use it as a rubber-duck / conversation partner for bigger picture issues. I'll run my code through it as a sanity "pre-check" before a pr review. And I mapped autocomplete to ctrl-; in vim so I only bring it up when I need it. Otherwise, I write everything myself.

Don't twist up in knots trying to get it to do decently what you can already do well yourself.
